note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a SA 5(1)-(3); A06b SA 5(1)-(3); L05 SA 6(1), 6(2)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. On 6 May 2025 the Constitutional Court confirmed the declaration that section 6(1)(a) of the Citizenship Act, under which a citizen lost South African citizenship on voluntarily acquiring another, is invalid (Democratic Alliance v Minister of Home Affairs, as EWN reported it the same day), so a South African now keeps it on taking another. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Democratic Alliance v Minister of Home Affairs and Another [2025] ZACC 8 (CCT 184/23), decided 6 May 2025, Constitutional Court of South Africa, judgment PDF from the Court's collections repository, Order paras 1-3. It confirmed loss on taking another citizenship. It was silent on the years of residence, renunciation, birth in the territory and descent, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.

sources.title: EWN, ConCourt confirms declaration of constitutional invalidity for parts of Citizenship Act (6 May 2025)
sources.said: The Constitutional Court has confirmed the declaration of constitutional invalidity of s 6(1)(a) of the Citizenship Act. The section stipulates that South African citizens lose their citizenship after voluntarily acquiring the citizenship of another country.

sources.title: Democratic Alliance v Minister of Home Affairs and Another [2025] ZACC 8 (CCT 184/23), decided 6 May 2025, Constitutional Court of South Africa, judgment PDF from the Court's collections repository, Order paras 1-3
sources.said: Citizenship Act 88 of 1995 — confirmation application — constitutionality of section 6(1)(a) — loss of citizenship — order of constitutional invalidity confirmed ... 2. It is declared that section 6(1)(a) of the South African Citizenship Act 88 of 1995 is inconsistent with the Constitution and is invalid from its promulgation on 6 October 1995. 3. It is further declared that those citizens who lost their citizenship by operation of section 6(1)(a) of the South African Citizenship Act 88 of 1995 are deemed not to have lost their citizenship.
